html:
Every CPQ feature you will configure is ultimately a set of object relationships. A quote is a header whose lines point at price book entries which point at products; an approval writes audit rows; a contract spawns renewal opportunities; a billing schedule fans out into recognition rows. If you can read this graph, you can debug CPQ — because almost every CPQ failure is a relationship failure: a line whose quote is missing, a schedule without a source object, a renewal orphaned from its contract.

This module is Phase 03 of the Academy. It maps the standard objects Salesforce ships for quoting, the custom objects this project adds for discounting, recognition, renewals, and approvals, the custom fields that extend each standard object, and the platform event bus that decouples the pieces.

Learning objectives

  • Draw the ownership chain Quote → QuoteLineItem → PricebookEntry → Product2.
  • Explain the parent-child and lookup relationships that connect Opportunity, Quote, Contract, Order, and Asset.
  • Name the five custom objects (Discount_Schedule__c, Revenue_Schedule__c, Renewal_Opportunity__c, Approval_Log__c, Training_Question__c) and their key fields.
  • Recall the custom fields added to the standard objects (Account, Opportunity, Quote, QuoteLineItem, Contract, Order).
  • Describe the Revenue_Sync__e platform event and the fields of its payload.
  • Navigate the model with relationship SOQL (parent-to-child and child-to-parent).
  • Identify the data used by the Apex services and their boundary guards.
  • Contrast this standard + custom model with the SBQQ__ managed-package data model.
  • Produce an entity-relationship drawing for your own implementation.

The ownership spine: Quote → QuoteLineItem → PricebookEntry → Product2

The single most important chain in CPQ:

text
Product2 ──< PricebookEntry ──< QuoteLineItem >── Quote ──> Opportunity
  (what)         (how much)        (line)       (header)      (deal)

Each QuoteLineItem is a child of one Quote and points at one PricebookEntry; the entry resolves the Product2. This makes products shareable across many quotes while each quote keeps its own priced snapshot.

RelationshipTypeWhy it matters
Quote → OpportunityLookupRevenue context, ARR, stage
Quote → AccountLookupCustomer, region, CPQ enabled flag
Quote → QuoteLineItemMaster-DetailDeleting a quote deletes its lines
QuoteLineItem → PricebookEntryLookupResolves price and product family
PricebookEntry → Pricebook2Lookup (formula/rel)Book, currency
PricebookEntry → Product2Master-DetailFamily, name, SKU

Master-detail means cascade delete — the parent owns the child's lifecycle. QuoteLineItems cannot exist outside their quote, which is why they are so cheap to query: every line always has QuoteId, and every PricebookEntry always has Product2Id.

Tip — When a quote's totals look wrong, trace this spine first. The most common bug is a QuoteLineItem whose PricebookEntryId points at a product whose family or price book entry is inactive — the line updates silently, and only the quote total looks off.

Supporting objects: what quoting hands off to

Quoting never ends at the quote. The same header-level objects connect forward:

ObjectRelationship to QuoteWhat records it
OpportunityOpportunityIdDeal, stage, ARR__c, Is_Strategic__c
Contract (custom fields)Contract service creates it from the quoteTermed agreement, Auto_Renew__c, Uplift_Percent__c
OrderQuoteIdFulfillment lifecycle and ERP sync
Revenue_Schedule__cQuote__c / Contract__c / Order__cBilling and recognition rows
Renewal_Opportunity__cContract__cUpcoming renewal value and date
Approval_Log__cQuote__cAudit trail of approval decisions

Note the deliberate design here: Revenue_Schedule__c is the hub that bridges quote → contract → order, because one deal can produce a quote, then a contract, then a renewal, then an order — each with its own schedule rows.

Custom objects (the Academy's business logic)

These five custom objects carry the domain logic that the managed package usually hides. Know their fields cold — the exercises and mini projects use them:

Discount_Schedule__c — volume tier pricing

text
Discount_Type__c  Lower_Bound__c  Upper_Bound__c  Discount_Percent__c
Product_Family__c Active__c

Tiers match inclusively on [Lower_Bound__c, Upper_Bound__c]; a blank Product_Family__c is a global fallback; only Active__c = true rows are considered.

Revenue_Schedule__c — billing + recognition rows

text
Quote__c  Contract__c  Order__c  Account__c  Amount__c  Recognized_Amount__c
Recognition_Date__c  Recognition_Method__c  Status__c  Period__c

One deal produces one set of rows per source object, so the Period__c + source-lookup combination identifies a row.

Renewal_Opportunity__c — the renewal pipeline

text
Account__c  Contract__c  Renewal_Date__c  ARR__c  Uplift_Percent__c  Status__c

ARR__c already includes uplift (e.g. 3200 contract ARR + 10% uplift = 3520 renewal ARR).

Approval_Log__c — approval audit trail

text
Quote__c  Approval_Type__c  Approver__c  Decision__c  Discount_Percent__c
Comments__c  Decision_Date__c

Appended on every approval action; later modules use it to route by discount threshold.

Training_Question__c — the exam question bank

text
Question_Text__c  Answer_Option_A__c..E__c  Correct_Answer__c  Explanation__c
Exam_Domain__c  Blueprint_Weight__c  Certification_Target__c  Difficulty__c  Is_Active__c

This is the data behind the certification-prep and quiz modules — one record per practice question, tagged with the official blueprint weight.

Custom fields on the standard objects

The Academy extends the six standard objects with the fields every implementation will recognize:

ObjectCustom fieldsUsed by
AccountCurrent_ARR__c, Region__c, Partner_Tier__c, Renewal_Risk__c, CPQ_Enabled__cARR rollup, routing, eligibility

QuoteApproval_Status__c, Discount_Percent__c, Contract_Term_Months__c, Is_Renewal__c, CPQ_Sync_Status__c, Total_ARR__c, Uplift_Percent__cApproval, pricing, renewal, sync
QuoteLineItemDiscount_Percent__c, List_Unit_Price__c, Net_Unit_Price__c, ARR__c, Is_Bundle_Parent__c, Bundle_Option__cPricing, configuration, ARR
ContractARR__c, Auto_Renew__c, Renewal_Term_Months__c, Uplift_Percent__c, CPQ_Contract_Status__cRenewals, contract sync

The hard rule for the exercises: do not invent other fields. When the hands-on tasks ask for a quote discount or a schedule period, use these exact names so the shared answers.js and the grading scripts keep working.

The event bus: Revenue_Sync__e

Platform events decouple the pipeline. Revenue_Sync__e is the shared notification contract:

text
Source_Object__c  Payload__c  Direction__c  Status__c  Correlation_Id__c
Integration_Type__c  Retry_Count__c  Endpoint__c

A real example from QuoteTriggerHandlerService.afterUpdate — when Approval_Status__c changes, one event is published per quote:

apex
events.add(new Revenue_Sync__e(
    Source_Object__c  = 'Quote',
    Direction__c      = 'Outbound',
    Integration_Type__c = 'ApprovalSync',
    Endpoint__c       = 'RevenueCloudEventBus',
    Correlation_Id__c = String.valueOf(Crypto.getRandomLong()),
    Payload__c        = JSON.serialize(new Map<String, Object>{
        'quoteId'        => q.Id,
        'approvalStatus' => q.Approval_Status__c,
        'totalArr'       => q.Total_ARR__c,
        'discountPercent'=> q.Discount_Percent__c
    })
));
json
{
  "sourceObject": "Quote",
  "direction": "Outbound",
  "integrationType": "ApprovalSync",
  "status": "Approved",
  "payload": {
    "quoteId": "0Q0...",
    "approvalStatus": "Approved",
    "totalArr": 3200.00,
    "discountPercent": 20.00
  }
}

The pattern is fire-and-forget: subscribers (an event-trigger, a downstream flow, an integration) react without the publisher blocking. @TestVisible lastPublishedEvents gives tests a stable assertion point without polling the bus.

Legacy note: the SBQQ__ data model in contrast

The managed package models the same domain with namespaced objects: SBQQ__Quote__c, SBQQ__QuoteLine__c, SBQQ__ProductOption__c, SBQQ__ProductFeature__c, SBQQ__PriceRule__c, SBQQ__DiscountSchedule__c, SBQQ__ConfigurationRule__c. The conceptual mapping is tight:

ConceptThis projectManaged package (SBQQ)
Quote headerQuote + custom fieldsSBQQ__Quote__c
Quote lineQuoteLineItem + custom fieldsSBQQ__QuoteLine__c
Bundle optionBundle_Option__c on the lineSBQQ__Option__c records under features
Discount tierDiscount_Schedule__cSBQQ__DiscountSchedule__c
Price rulePriceRuleEngineService (Apex)SBQQ__PriceRule__c records
Approval auditApproval_Log__cPartially SBQQ__Quote__c fields

This is the only place SBQQ__ object names appear in the Academy content — you need them to translate between the two engines, not to build on them.

Hands-on walkthrough

This walkthrough builds the relationship graph with real SOQL and then subjects it to the service layer.

  1. Draw the ERD first, on paper: Opportunity 1─1 Quote 1─N QuoteLineItem N─1 PricebookEntry N─1 Product2; Quote 1─1 Contract; Contract 1─N Renewal_Opportunity__c; Quote 1─N Revenue_Schedule__c 1─1 Account; Quote 1─N Approval_Log__c. Then prove it exists in the org.
  2. Prove the ownership spine with a parent-to-line query:

    soql
    SELECT Id, Name, Total_ARR__c,
       (SELECT Id, Product2.Name, Product2.Family, Quantity, Net_Unit_Price__c
        FROM QuoteLineItems)
FROM Quote
WHERE Total_ARR__c > 0

    The inner QuoteLineItems relationship returns lines without a second query — master-detail at work.

  3. Resolve the products behind the lines (child-to-parent via the price book entry):

    soql
    SELECT QuoteId, PricebookEntryId, PricebookEntry.Product2.Name,
       PricebookEntry.Product2.Family, Quantity, Net_Unit_Price__c
FROM QuoteLineItem
WHERE PricebookEntry.Product2.IsActive = true

  4. Query the full contract-to-renewal graph:

    soql
    SELECT Id, ContractTerm, ARR__c, Uplift_Percent__c, Auto_Renew__c,
       (SELECT ARR__c, Renewal_Date__c, Status__c FROM Renewal_Opportunities__r)
FROM Contract
WHERE Status = 'Draft'

  5. Verify the schedule fan-out — one deal, three sources, each with rows:

    soql
    SELECT Quote__c, Contract__c, Order__c, Period__c, Recognition_Method__c, Status__c
FROM Revenue_Schedule__c
ORDER BY Period__c

  6. Hit the service layer. Reset totals on every quote your queries returned, then confirm nothing throws on a null batch — the boundary guards are part of the contract:

    apex
    Set<Id> quoteIds = new Set<Id>();
for (Quote q : [SELECT Id FROM Quote WHERE Total_ARR__c > 0]) { quoteIds.add(q.Id); }
QuoteCalculatorService.recalculateTotals(quoteIds);          // one query + one update
QuoteCalculatorService.recalculateTotals(null);               // must not throw
System.assertEquals(0, BundleConfigurationService.validateBundleConfiguration(null).size());
  7. Watch the event contract fire. Update any quote's Approval_Status__c and confirm exactly one Revenue_Sync__e exists with Source_Object__c = 'Quote' and a JSON Payload__c — your parseable bridge to downstream systems.

Common pitfalls

  • Assuming every relation is master-detail. Quote→Opportunity and line→entry are lookups; deleting the opportunity leaves the quote orphaned with a broken OpportunityId.
  • Querying in a loop inside a service. Loading Revenue_Schedule__c per quote in a 200-quote batch burns the 100-query governor. Always gather the parent Set<Id> first (bulk-safe pattern).
  • Typo'd custom field names. List_Unit_Price__c is not ListUnitPrice__c. The exercises grade on the exact field names in this guide.
  • Schedules without a source. A Revenue_Schedule__c row with no Quote__c, Contract__c, or Order__c is unreachable by every service. Give every row a source.
  • Overwriting approval state. QuoteTriggerHandlerService.beforeUpdate preserves the existing Approval_Status__c rather than wiping it — your own handlers should never clobber state they don't own.
  • Confusing ARR value with recognition. Account.Current_ARR__c only changes when Revenue_Schedule__c rows are recognized, not when a quote is signed.

Key takeaways

  • The spine Quote → QuoteLineItem → PricebookEntry → Product2 is the first thing to trace when quoting goes wrong.
  • Five custom objects carry the domain logic: Discount_Schedule__c, Revenue_Schedule__c, Renewal_Opportunity__c, Approval_Log__c, Training_Question__c.
  • Standard objects are extended with precise custom fields — use exactly these names in exercises and mini projects.
  • Revenue_Sync__e decouples the pipeline with JSON payloads and correlation IDs; one "approved" event can drive every downstream integration.
  • Every Apex service owns one slice of the graph and never throws on empty input — that is the bulk/factory safety contract.
  • The conceptual SBQQ__ mapping exists so you can translate between classic CPQ and this standard + custom model.
  • With the graph in your head, the next phases (bundles and price rules) become small: rules just read and write this data model.
